definitions.explanation: A person who eats a large amount of food. The final character {漢|かん} means "man," so the word originally referred to men, but it is now used loosely for anyone who eats a lot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{大食漢|たいしょくかん}だ。
examples.english: My younger brother is a big eater.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{大食漢|たいしょくかん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦おかわり→おかわり：10967_okawari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He is a big eater and always gets seconds.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{大食漢|たいしょくかん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{一度|いちど}→一度：01312_ichido⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{五人前|ごにんまえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{平|たい}らげる。
examples.english: That athlete is a famous big eater who polishes off five servings at once.

notes:
Written {大|たい} (big) + {食|しょく} (eat) + {漢|かん} (man). A somewhat literary or descriptive word, often used admiringly or humorously.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{大食|おおぐ}い→大食い：08341_oogui⟧: big eating; a big eater — more colloquial; also names the competitive-eating sense
- {健啖家|けんたんか}: hearty eater — more refined, emphasizes a healthy appetite
- ⟦{食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}→食いしん坊：16180_kuishinbou⟧: glutton; foodie — casual, suggests loving food rather than sheer quantity
